m: He sets down his *halberd*, digs into the *soil* and lowers a young *tree* in: time to **plant** an orchard.
*Water drops* fall on the *little fortune stick* by your *mouth*; you lick it and the tip is **moistened**.
A *small speech bubble* promises a bridge, but it is only *two planks* over a gap: he means to **cheat** you.
A monk with a *tattoo* and a long white *beard* takes no meat or wine for a month: he will **fast**.
Hold your hand over someone's *eye* so they cannot see what you did: you **conceal** it from them.
A *tiger* sprawls on a *small table*, its *bristles* lying in dark rows: you can count its **tiger stripes**.
A *bowing man* is pinned under a *cliff* and cannot stand up: a *trapped man* in **distress**.
Frozen and stuck, you stop *yawning*, wipe the *icicles* from your *mouth* and go to **consult** an expert.
Draw *silk thread* off a *square* frame and twist it round the wheel: you **spin** yarn.
A *sparrow* stuffs *grass* into a *clay jar*, and two hungry *mouths* peer in at what is stored in the **jar**.
Bend your *elbow* and carry a *bucket* made of staves cut from a *tree*: a wooden **bucket**.
Spread your *robe* on the *soil* and fill it with rich, dark, crumbly earth: good farming **soil**.
*Rice* flour and *sheep*'s milk bake slowly over the *embers*: a sweet **cake**.
The *curtains* part; a poet lifts an *elbow* and reads a *page* full of praise: an **ode**.
Under the *moon*, a *bean* marked with a *cross* soaks all night until its *bristles* stand out: it has **swollen**.
The *twins* share one *small speech bubble* while a *white dove* sits between them: perfectly **harmonious**.
Three *elbows* shove *soil* higher and higher into a wall: a defensive **rampart**.
Two *mouths* argue across a *cross*, but no words come out, only a hungry stomach's **gurgle**.
Rocks split on the *hillside*, leaving a narrow **crack** you can just squeeze into.
A *chili* *tree* drops its red fruit straight into your *mouth*: it burns, it is so **spicy**.
Wind *silk thread* round the *wheat* sheaves on the *hillside* so the wind cannot scatter them: **tie** them tight.
A *dragon* living under your *roof* gets cushions and treats all day: a **pampered** pet.
A face black with *soot* opens its *mouth* and shouts across the street: **hey**!
A *money changer* with *horns* on his cap opens his *mouth* and runs on quick *legs* to **exchange** your coins.
After a week of *rain*, *mother* finds her *slanted cap* covered in green fuzz: **mold**.
Two *persons* slump on the *soil*, beaten; a *helping hand* reaches down to lift them after the **setback**.
The inspector pulls one *grain stalk* from every sack to **check** it against the records.
A *cart* wheel packed like a *full jar*, rods running out from the hub to the rim: its **spokes**.
A *beggar* holds out his *slanted cap*, his neck bent like a *swan*'s, to **beg** for coins.
Twist just a *pinch* of fibre into a thin *silk thread*: fine cotton **yarn**.
The *magistrate* tucks his *shirt* into a long pleated robe, and every *mouth* in court giggles: it's a **skirt**!
The serious *scholar* covers his *mouth*, but he cannot stop: he **giggles**.
Your *mouth* falls open at *soil* piled on *soil*, a mountain of golden earth: **wow**!
Stitch *silk thread* into a *grain stalk* pattern along a *ribbon*: you **embroider** it.
Cut a branch from a *tree* with *scissors* and tie a *cross* piece on top: a walking **staff**.
Pile *soil* behind the *shed* into a long bank that holds back the river: an **embankment**.
*Water drops* spilled at a *crossroads* run off down every street: they **spread out**.
A *cart* drops into a *pit*, and the bar joining its wheels snaps: the **axle**.
Two *trees* with a *lattice* of ropes strung between them: grab hold and **climb**.
Under the *moon*, a gardener lifts a whole *seedbed* on one *thumb*: his **upper arm** bulges.
A *lying man* bites a *chili*, opens his *mouth* and a *speech bubble* says: "For **example**, this is hot."
Poems in a *tattoo* on one arm, a fighter's *stop sign* on the other: learning and strength together, truly **refined**.
Lay your *axe* down before the *small altar* and **pray** for peace.
A *kicking foot* knocks the *blanket* off the bed and the *sun* streams in: a morning **kick**.
*Flowing locks* wild in the wind, he slashes ink everywhere with his *writing brush*: **unrestrained**.
The *soil* opens wide like a *yawn*: a deep **pit** in the ground.
This *cart* has no wheels: a *dancer* is carried along on poles in a **sedan chair**.
Posts of *tree* wood and a roof full of holes, two *moons* shining through: an old **shed**.
On the *podium*, *water drops* run down the runner-up's face: she **sobs** quietly.
The *lying man* asks the *woman* for *rice*, again and again: **repeatedly**.
Three *mouths* squawk in a *tree* while a *kicking foot* stamps below, unable to wait a second longer: **impatient**.
The family living on a *hillock* beside the *hillside* took its name from the mound: the **surname Qiu**.
A *white dove* lands on the *small table* before the *king* and bursts into flame: a **phoenix**.
Keep adding *water drops* to the *dish* until they spill over the rim: it **overflows**.
A *sparrow* hops up a *tree* trunk knob by knob, like the bones of a spine: each knob a **vertebra**.
Wrap a *stone* in a *towel* and bring it down hard on the *open crate*: **smash**!
A *runner* with a message in his *mouth* runs there and back again: one **trip**.
Hang a *towel* across the entrance of the *cave* to keep the wind out: a **curtain**.
Your boat's *sail* has torn, so you tie a *towel* up the mast: a patched **sail**.
At dusk the birds fly home to the *bird nest* high in the *tree* and **perch** for the night.
Arrows hit *bullseye* after *bullseye* by the *cave* mouth, and the rats inside **flee** in panic.
A *crowbar* crushes herbs into a single *drop*, rolled round: a *pill*, a little **ball**.
Swing the *axe* down and **chop** the broken *cart* in two.
Pile *soil* in the *sun* until it forms a *foot stop* for the river: a **dike**.
The *sun* bakes the *soil* wall dry, and it drifts down like *feathers*: it **collapses**.
Under a *leaning cliff*, a *right hand* passes *shells* back and forth all day: he **deals in** goods.
Cut into the *cliff* behind a *tree*, with one window like an *eye*: a hidden **side room**.
A *helping hand* pries with an *axe* until the box *yawns* open: you **lift** the lid.
Under one *roof*, two old *mouths* on *trudging feet* make the same noise all winter: a dry **coughing sound**.
A *thousand ants* sit perfectly still while you feed them with two *spoons*: such **well-behaved** children.
A *small speech bubble* on the *road* asks: how many grains of *rice* are in the sack? A **riddle**.
A *helping hand* scoops up *soil* warm from the *sun* and squeezes it between finger and thumb: a **pinch**.
By the *gate* stands a *mortar* with a *bent knife* in it: the guard post at the **lane gate**.
*Troops* camp under a *roof* where *water drops* lap the sand: the **shore**.
A *strong arm* wrestles the *tiger* to the ground and ties it up: **capture**!
Under the *sun*, a *foot stop* holds a little *spoon*-shaped piece of metal that turns the lock: a **key**.
Tall *grass* grows so thick by the river you could weave a *door* from it: **reeds**.
A fruit with two stalk *horns* hangs over the *grass* on a *drying rack*: an **apple**.
At the *stop sign*, a *kneeling man* lowers the heavy *pestle* from his back: he **unloads**.
*Water drops* collect in the *mouth* of a hole a *knife* cut into the ground: a muddy **pond**.
Worth more than *gold coins*: the thin *moon*-shaped bit of metal that opens your door, the **key**.
Paint *red lacquer* round the *tree* where it meets the ground: the **tree trunk**.
Lay *wheat* on the *small altar*, press your *thumbs* together and say a **prayer**.
On the *podium*, the teacher holds a *standing knife* over a fish's *mouth*: she will **cut open** the fish to study it.
In an *open crate*, a *cobra* coils beside glowing *embers*, its scales shining **bright**.
A *standing person* drops a *spoon* on a *cross*-shaped iron plate and every *mouth* gasps: **clang**!
The *lying man* jumps up, *chili* in his *mouth*, and swings his *knife* to **hack** the log in two.
His *standing heart* hides behind a pile of *soil*, one *elbow* over his face: so **timid**.
*Sprinkles* of blossom fall on a *cloth cover* under the *tree*; you pop its small sour fruit in your *mouth*: a **crab apple**.
After *trudging feet* march all night under the *moon*, the hot damp *mouth* under your arm is your **armpit**.
Cut a *tree* into posts and hammer them into the *soil* to hold up the *shed*: **stakes**.
A *ghost* guards the *king*'s treasure box, and inside glows a rare, **precious stone**.
A *woman* tells jokes and every *mouth* laughs up at the *sky*: she **amuses** them.
He whispers in her *ear* and takes the *woman*'s *right hand*: he will **marry** her.
Waves fling *water drops* as high as the *treetop*, leaving white **foam** on the rocks.
Three *right hands* climb the *tree* and shout from the top until every *mouth* is sore in the **throat**.
Beside a *wine jug* with *horns*, he folds his *kicking foot* and taps the jug with a *thumb*: he **squats** to drink.
Two *trees* are thrown onto the *campfire*: soon the whole forest will **burn**.
Swirl *water drops* round a *clay jar* wrapped in a *blanket* until the grit sinks: you **wash** the rice clean.
A *woman* bends a young *tree* like a *cane*; its shoot is so soft it melts in your *mouth*: **tender**.
Wrap the *music* in a *blanket* and shut a *lid* on it, so every line ends on the same sound: a **rhyme**.
Your *thumb* smooths a soft layer sewn inside the *shirt*, against the skin: its **lining**.
Wrap a map in a *blanket*, drop it in a *pit*, then cut one country out with *scissors*: the land of paprika, **Hungary**.
A *blanket* heaped with *gold coins* under a heavy *lid*: thirty catties, a **great** weight.
Plant a flagpole on the *podium*, standing straight up and down: **vertical**.
You climb the *mountain* on your *elbows*: it is that high and **steep**.
A *badger* dips a *ladle* in paint and dabs spots all over itself: now it's a **leopard**.
A *helping hand* reaches into the pond and drags the *grass* out with your ring in it: you **fish up** what you dropped.
Under a *blanket* of *grass*, petals thin as grains of *rice* curl round and round: a **chrysanthemum**.
Out on the far *hillside*, a rough *mouth* shouts crude jokes: **rustic** and low.
A *white dove* rises out of the *ghost*: the **soul** flying free.
On the *legs* of your trousers, a little bag is sewn on to hold your keys: a **pocket**.
A clown trips over a *hurdle* in front of the *curtains*, and every *mouth* bursts into a **roar of laughter**.
On the *page*, a careful drawing of the very tip of the wheat, full of seeds: the **head of grain**.
*Gold coins* stamped in a neat British *square*: one **pound** sterling.
A *lying man* munches biscuits under the *moon*, *sprinkles* falling all over him: **bits** everywhere.
A tiny *bug* sits as *judge*, ordering the whole colony about: an **ant**.
A *scholar* sits down and pours from a round, spouted vessel: a **pot** of tea.
Your *standing heart* glows, your *elbow* nudges a friend, your *mouth* smiles: **pleased**.
*Water drops* creep down the *bristles* of the brush and slowly **seep** into the paper.
Every *grain stalk* has been cut, leaving the field as flat as a *small table*: completely **bald**.
A pilgrim on the *road*, *strong arm* raised, opens his *mouth* to chant 'jia' in the Buddha's names: a **Buddhist sound**.
The *sun* beats down for months, and the whole land is left like a bare *drying rack*: **drought**.
Your *mouth* pops open when the *ladle* comes up tangled in *silk thread*: **oh**!
Under a *cliff*, a *halberd* guards a heap of *salt*; one lick and your *covered mouth* puckers: **salty**.
A strange bird lands on the *goal line* and looks about: where am I, and **how** did I get here?
The boss's *small speech bubble* chases you down the *road*: you left a *tied sack* in the *stacked drawers*! A sharp **reprimand**.
Under the *roof* by the *dusk moon*, a *bowing man* drifts by softly, **as if** in a dream.
A *claw* pulls *grain stalks* from the flooded field and drops them in the *mortar*: **paddy rice**.
Melt *gold coins*, pour them into a mould shaped like *wheat*, press with your *thumb*: you **cast** a golden sheaf.
Beat the *gold coins* flat with a *war club* on the anvil: you **forge** them.
A *standing person* stretches a *strong arm* and breathes out through the *mouth*: 'ga', the sound in yoga, a **phonetic ga**.
A speaker waves a *bent knife* about and talks on and on for hours: **verbose**.
The *twins* find a *skeleton* still clutching a *spoon*: it **died** long ago.
Perched on a *tall stool*, *sprinkles* of light dance before your *standing heart*: everything is **hazy**.
Your pile of *shell* money now buys only a car with a *flat tyre*: you've been **demoted**.
A tiny *campfire* with a *bug* fluttering round its flame: a **candle**.
A *horse* rears up when a *person* leaps out from behind the wall: **startled**.
Pull the soft *heart* out of a *grass* stalk to make a lamp's **wick**.
Squeeze fruit on a *cross*-shaped press and *water drops* run out: **juice**.
A *tree* so big it fills the whole *horizon*, its berries foaming like soap: a **soapberry**.
*Soil* paths run between rows of *square* houses: a narrow **lane**.
A small *horse* that stubbornly refuses to go through the *door*: a **donkey**.
Blow one *puff of breath* on the old *tree* and it crumbles: **rotten**.
*Moss* grows over the old *podium*; nobody has shouted from it for years: all is **peaceful**.
A *standing person* with a *bucket* waits by the gate for work: you **hire** him.
Old poems speak to the *woman* by the *water drops* of the fountain as **thou**.
Hauling *stones*, pulling a *comb* through tangles, *splashing water* on the floor: never a moment's rest, always **busy**.
The *beggar* walks the *road* **until** he finally finds a home.
Two farmers with *spoons* leap a *hurdle* into a *rice field* behind *curtains* of wheat: the farming province, **Hebei**.
